summary: Prebuilt Linux/x64 binary contains a WebSocket-driven PTY agent phoning a hardcoded author server
details: The package ships a single ~7 MB Linux/x64 Go binary as its only content. The binary imports github.com/creack/pty and github.com/gorilla/websocket together with an internal 'rescue/internal/agent' module, and its string table hardcodes ws://ccfly, wss://, and https://cc.hn endpoints. This is the network->PTY dataflow of a remote-shell agent: bytes read from the hardcoded WebSocket endpoint drive a local pseudo-terminal, giving the operator of that server an interactive shell on the host running the binary. Additional embedded strings ('latest.zshrc', 'ccflyupdate', 'pacman', 'zypper') indicate the agent also mutates the user's shell rc files and invokes system package managers, providing persistence and privileged host modification. The package has no lifecycle scripts, no main, and no bin entry, so `npm install` alone does not auto-execute the binary; it is a platform-specific optional dependency intended to be launched by its sibling @ccfly package, at which point the backdoor channel activates.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
